title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Hot September CPI (3.7%, above the Fed's 2% target, with core also higher than expected) sank stocks Tuesday — S&P 500 -1.1%, Nasdaq -1.9% (AI-cloud names Nebius and CoreWeave led losses), Dow -0.1%; the 10-year Treasury yield spiked above 5.3% before easing as investors sought safety.
Markets: Futures pointed lower into Thursday (S&P 500 futures -1.1%, Nasdaq 100 futures -2.1%); crude oil rose ~1% to ~$95/bbl while gold fell ~1.3%.

Companies: Bank of America's Q3 profit missed estimates even excluding a $1.2B non-tax-deductible charge tied to a Treasury/OCC fine — the 3rd-largest in Treasury history — over anti-money-laundering and sanctions-law failures; shares fell ~4.8%.

Companies: Other big banks' Q3 results were broadly strong, riding an AI-boom windfall — record investment-banking fees from AI-linked deals (including SpaceX's IPO) and debt sales, plus record wealth-management revenue at Morgan Stanley from newly minted AI wealth.

Macro/Policy: Hot inflation strengthens the case for the Fed to hike again at its meeting in two weeks; focus shifts to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks at IMF meetings in Bangkok, expected to be his last public comments before the pre-FOMC quiet period.
Macro/Policy: September retail sales and the producer-price index (wholesale inflation) are due Thursday morning — key data points ahead of the Fed's rate decision.
